monument_name: Rasipatan temple and stone memorial pillar
anglicized_name: Rasipatan temple and stone memorial pillar
name_devanagari: रसिपतन् मन्दिर र स्मृति खम्बा|| JUM0530
description_en: The temple and the pillar are located on the right banks of the Sinja River, by theghāṭa, south of Ludku village. The site is used for death rituals. It consists of two buildings. To the west is a newly constructed rest-house built with stones and cement and covered with CGI sheets.  On the south-east façade, to the left of the door, a stone memorial pillar is inserted. From the 13th to the 16th-17th centuries, stone memorial pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin. They are mostly erected to honour war heroes (Andolfatto 2019).The pillar (JUM0530-001) is in good condition and is adorned with a rosette surmounting an arrow-like motif. The lack of an inscription and the pillar's unique arrow-like motif make dating difficult. Therefore, one can only guess that it was made between the 13th and the 16th-17th centuries. A stone slab on the right side of the door bears an inscription from the Śaka era (the date itself is eroded).A small square stone temple built with roughly cut stone and mud masonry is located east of the rest-house. The door is oriented eastward. Its stone doorjambs are unadorned but appear to be relatively old, as indicated by their level of erosion. Opposite the entrance is a stepped sanctum, where aniconic stones are enshrined. The sanctum is covered with a corbelled vault. The monument appears to have been rebuilt over time. Its antiquity remains difficult to assess.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Repaired , Restored
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
